discovery: Discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and establishment of the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

nominees.name: Enrico Costa
nominees.affiliation: INAF - Istituto di Astrofisica e Planetologia Spaziali, Rome, Italy

nominees.name: Filippo Frontera
nominees.affiliation: University of Ferrara and INAF-OAS Bologna, Italy

motivation: For three decades the nature of gamma-ray bursts was one of the deepest mysteries in physics. In 1997, Costa and Frontera, using the BeppoSAX satellite, discovered the fading X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228, providing arcminute positions within hours. This enabled optical and radio follow-up; Kulkarni and collaborators measured the first redshifts and radio afterglows, proving that bursts arise at cosmological distances and are the most luminous explosions in the universe, with relativistic outflows confirmed through radio scintillation and expansion. These discoveries created the field of rapid time-domain astrophysics, led to the gamma-ray burst-supernova connection revealing the deaths of massive stars, made bursts probes of the earliest galaxies and reionization, and laid the scientific and observational foundation for the multi-messenger identification of the neutron-star merger GW170817 with a short gamma-ray burst and kilonova. They opened a new window on relativistic physics in the cosmos.
